topic: the 1915 cocoa-pod mix-up behind Coca-Cola's contour bottle shape
title: Coca-Cola's Bottle Shape Came From a Cocoa-Pod Mistake
description: AI-narrated commentary on the real story behind Coca-Cola's iconic bottle shape -- a 1915 design mix-up that's still baked into every bottle today.

hook_candidates.text: Coca-Cola's most famous bottle shape has a cocoa-pod mistake baked right in.
The Coca-Cola bottle wasn't designed to look like a woman's body. It was a mix-up.
Ever wonder why the Coca-Cola bottle has ridges? Nobody meant to put them there.
In 1915, two men sketched the wrong plant, and it became Coca-Cola's bottle.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who insists Coca-Cola's bottle was designed to look sexy, because they want to prove it was actually just a mix-up.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume Coca-Cola's iconic bottle shape came from pure design genius, not a mistake.
closing_comment: Wildest part: Coca-Cola's bottle shape comes from a cocoa-pod, and cocoa isn't even in the drink.

sources.note: Company history confirms 1915 designers found a cocoa pod picture in an encyclopedia while researching the coca leaf and kola nut.
National Archives blog confirms the original wider prototype didn't fit bottling equipment and had to be narrowed before production.
